Military officials say at least four people were killed and 39 injured, 19 of them critically
in the explosion and fire at a Canadian Forces base in Alberta over the weekend.
Dan Karp and Chuck reports.
Major General L. W. Rettland says officials at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright were aware
of a grass fire for several hours before it quickly spread to the training area where
training activities were underway.
He says the fire was about three quarters of a mile from the troops, but because of
what he described as uncommonly strong winds, it reached the exercise area in less than
a minute.
The Defense Department says there are no indications that this was a terrorist attack.
Rettland says there will be a board of inquiry, but because of the number of casualties and
complexities it could take some time.
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the nation is in mourning after what he called one of
the worst tragedies for the Canadian military in peacetime.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karp and Chuck in Toronto.
President Trump says Israel's embattled prime minister has his complete and total endorsement
in upcoming Israeli elections.
The endorsement is a boost for Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu, who in NPR's Emily Fang reports
is facing serious questions yet again about his handling of several wars.
Citing Israel's support for the ongoing war in Iran, Trump wrote that without Netanyahu,
America would "have to do this work ourselves."
Netanyahu responded by video that he was honored and humbled, and he needs all the political
help he can get, as Israel prepares to vote at the end of the month.
The latest polls show Netanyahu trailing behind opposition candidate Gaddy Eisenkot.
Recent reporting also alleges Netanyahu ignored repeated warnings from various Arab intelligence
officials before Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023.
Netanyahu's managed to survive criticism of that security failure, but that and the
fallout from Israel's war in Gaza has turned this election into one of the most consequential
in Israel's history.
Emily Fang and Pure News, Washington.
President Trump continues his campaign rallies for GOP candidates this week.
On Monday, he'll be in Kansas, and with the midterm elections nearing, NPR's Marlaison
reports that Democratic candidates are raising more money than the Republican opponents.
All through this election cycle, Republican campaign committees and billionaire super PACs
have been swamping their Democratic equivalents.
Elon Musk, for instance, has spent more than $150 million in Texas to help the Republican
Senate candidate there, Ken Paxton.
But according to the latest campaign finance filings, Paxton's Democratic opponent, James
Tallarico, raised six times as much as Paxton himself this quarter.
Donations to individual candidates are usually a good proxy for voter enthusiasm, and this
year the enthusiasm gap favors Democrats.
Democratic candidates in other key Senate races, including Alaska, Ohio, Maine, Michigan,
and Iowa, have also outraised their Republican opponents.
Marlaison, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The Russian Defense Ministry says its forces carried out a massive strike Monday on targets
in Ukraine's capital region.
In a statement it says the attack targeted military industrial facilities, storage sites
for missiles and drones, and data centers.
If confirmed, the strike comes one day after Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at
Russia, hitting sites as far away as St. Petersburg.
Time is running out for registering to vote for the midterm elections in some states.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has this rundown of the latest upcoming deadlines.
The window closes today for eligible voters to register or update their registration in
Alabama, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota.
And there's less than a week left until the next major voter registration deadline on Saturday.
That's in Massachusetts and New York.
Before you know it, it will be Halloween on October 31, which is also the last day in
North Carolina for signing up in person at the state's early voting sites.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's official election
website to confirm your status and contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their
name, or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.

The Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything pulled in an impressive $15 million
